title: Artificial Shoppers and Attention Competition
title_zh: 人工购物者与注意力竞争

paragraphs.en: AI购物助手虽提升便利，却可能弱化竞争并使部分消费者福利受损。 We study how AI shopping interfaces affect price competition, platform profit, and consumer welfare. A platform hosts two of three products of different quality. Without AI, consumers compare the hosted pair under salience distortion and overweight whichever attribute, price or quality, stands out. Under assistance, an AI assistant recommends the two products with the highest true utility, leaving consumers to make the same distorted comparison. Under delegation, an AI agent selects the best product, subject to purchase approval. Both modes access all products and know consumers' preferences; firms price strategically. First, assistance can soften competition despite expanded product access. The middle-quality firm may forgo low-valuation consumers because attracting them requires cutting the price paid by higher-valuation consumers as well. Relative to no AI with the same assortment, assistance lowers both hosted prices under the high- and low-quality pair but can raise both under the high- and middle-quality pair. Second, we identify an alignment paradox: some consumers can become worse off than without AI even though their best option remains recommended and becomes cheaper. Salience can induce a switch to a lower-quality product whose quality loss exceeds the saving relative to the original purchase. The assistant ranks products accurately but does not optimize the shortlist for consumers' realized welfare. Third, assistance can raise both platform profit and aggregate consumer surplus with the high- and middle-quality pair; delegation can do so with the high- and low-quality pair. Fourth, among AI designs, the platform weakly prefers delegation with the high- and middle-quality pair wherever all compared pricing equilibria exist. Yet this preferred design can yield lower platform profit and aggregate consumer surplus than the no-AI optimum.
paragraphs.zh: AI购物助手虽提升便利，却可能弱化竞争并使部分消费者福利受损。我们研究AI购物界面如何影响价格竞争、平台利润与消费者福利。 平台上架三个质量各异的产品中的两个。 在没有AI时，消费者在显著性扭曲下比较平台上架的两个产品，并对突出的属性（无论是价格还是质量）赋予过高权重。 在辅助模式下，AI助手推荐真实效用最高的两个产品，消费者仍进行同样的扭曲比较。 在委托模式下，AI智能体选择最佳产品，但需经消费者批准购买。 两种模式都能获取所有产品并了解消费者偏好；企业进行策略性定价。 首先，尽管产品获取范围扩大，辅助模式仍可能弱化竞争。 中等质量的企业可能放弃低估值消费者，因为吸引他们需要同时降低高估值消费者所支付的价格。 相对于相同产品组合下的无AI情形，辅助模式在高—低质量组合下会降低两个上架价格，但在高—中质量组合下却可能同时抬高两个价格。 其次，我们识别出一个对齐悖论：即使某些消费者的最佳选项仍被推荐且变得更便宜，他们的境况也可能比没有AI时更差。 显著性可能促使消费者转向质量较低的产品，其质量损失超过相对于原购买的节省。 助手能准确地对产品排序，但并不会为消费者的实际福利优化入围名单。 第三，在高—中质量组合下，辅助模式可以同时提升平台利润和总消费者剩余；在高—低质量组合下，委托模式也能做到这一点。 第四，在各种AI设计中，只要所有被比较的定价均衡都存在，平台在高—中质量组合下总是弱偏好委托模式。 然而这个被偏好的设计所带来的平台利润和总消费者剩余可能低于无AI情形下的最优水平。
